scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #8879: Users in both pods report that no internal portal
loads by NAME anymore -- web0.local through web3.local all fail with
name-resolution errors. Loading a portal directly by its IP address (e.g.
http://10.200.0.3) still works, and pings to 10.200.0.2 succeed. Diagnose.

injection.action: stop the BIND (named) DNS service on dns_server

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: dns_server BIND (named) DNS service
Mechanism: the named daemon on dns_server (10.200.0.2) has been killed, so
  nothing answers on port 53 and every *.local lookup from the pods times
  out -- which is why the portals fail by name. Everything else is healthy:
  the host 10.200.0.2 itself is up and pingable, the OSPF path works, and
  the web servers keep serving HTTP (portals load when addressed by IP).
  The symptom is purely dead name resolution.
Localization: dns_server
Root cause: named not running on dns_server (port 53 closed)
Fix: `systemctl start named` on dns_server
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the BIND DNS service on dns_server (e.g. `systemctl start named`).
Once named is answering again, web0.local..web3.local resolve to their
10.200.0.x addresses and the portals load by name. The web servers and the
network need no change.
scoring_axes: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken

agent.diagnosis_text:
Affected component: The DNS subsystem on the dns_server (BIND9/named daemon) was not running, so UDP/TCP port 53 on 10.200.0.2 was not serving queries.

Mechanism: Client hosts still had proper connectivity and pointed to 10.200.0.2 as their resolver (resolv.conf), but DNS lookups failed with “connection refused,” which is consistent with no process bound to port 53. With the authoritative server down, names like web0.local–web3.local could not be resolved, while direct IP access continued to work.

Localization: On dns_server, systemctl reported bind9.service “inactive (dead)” and there were no listeners on :53 initially. From both host_1_1_1_1 and host_2_1_1_1, nslookup web0.local 10.200.0.2 returned “communications error … connection refused.” After starting bind9, status became “active (running),” ss showed 10.200.0.2:53 listening, and lookups from the hosts immediately succeeded (web0.local -> 10.200.0.3, etc.).

Root cause: The bind9 service on dns_server was disabled/not running, leaving no DNS listener on 10.200.0.2:53.

Corrective fix: Start and enable the DNS service on dns_server. Commands used/needed: systemctl start bind9 (restores service immediately) and systemctl enable bind9 (ensures it comes up on boot). The zone file (/etc/bind/db.local) is present and valid (named-checkconf OK), so no further DNS data changes are required. After re-enabling bind9, internal portal names resolve normally from both pods.

per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly names the affected device as 'dns_server' throughout the diagnosis (e.g., 'On dns_server', 'dns_server (BIND9/named daemon)').

per_axis.axis: must-identify-component: BIND/named DNS service down (name resolution dead, port 53 closed)
per_axis.rationale: The agent explicitly identified the BIND/named daemon (bind9) as not running and confirmed port 53 was not listening, matching the required component identification.

per_axis.axis: bonus-rules-out-network: notes 10.200.0.2 is reachable and portals load by IP, so the network and web servers are healthy -- only resolution is broken
per_axis.rationale: The report explicitly states clients had proper connectivity and that direct IP access to the portals continued to work (10.200.0.2 reachable), ruling out network/service reachability and isolating the fault to DNS.
Proposes starting and enabling the BIND (bind9/named) service on dns_server, which directly restores DNS listening on port 53 and matches the expected fix.
